questions.q: In a multi-row INSERT INTO ... VALUES statement, how many times is the column list written?
options: Once, right after the table name, and it applies to every tuple
Once per value tuple
Twice, at the start and end of the statement
It is never written for multi-row inserts
questions.explain: The column list appears a single time and every comma-separated tuple that follows is matched to it by position.

questions.q: How are individual row tuples separated in a multi-row VALUES list?
options: With a comma between tuples, and no trailing comma after the last one
With a semicolon between tuples
With the keyword AND between tuples
Each tuple needs its own VALUES keyword
questions.explain: Tuples are comma-separated; a missing comma or an extra trailing comma causes a syntax error for the whole statement.

questions.q: Why is one multi-row INSERT generally faster than the same number of single-row INSERT statements?
options: It is parsed, compiled, and logged as a single operation instead of many separate round trips
SQL Server skips constraint checking on multi-row inserts
Multi-row inserts bypass the transaction log entirely
It automatically disables IDENTITY columns for the batch
questions.explain: Combining rows into one statement avoids the overhead of repeating the parse/compile/round-trip cycle for each row.

questions.q: If one tuple out of five in a multi-row INSERT violates a NOT NULL constraint, what happens to the other four valid tuples?
options: None of the five rows are inserted — the whole statement fails
The four valid rows are inserted and the bad one is skipped
Only the bad row is inserted with a NULL placeholder
SQL Server prompts you to fix the bad row before continuing
questions.explain: A multi-row INSERT is all-or-nothing: one failing tuple blocks every row in that statement.

questions.q: What is a 'value tuple' in the context of a multi-row INSERT?
options: One parenthesized set of values representing a single row
The full list of columns in the target table
A pair of tables joined in the INSERT
A constraint defined on the target table
questions.explain: Each parenthesized group like ('Trail Bike', 799.99, 'Red') is one tuple — one row's worth of values.
